labels.label: [7.0] the achronal domain Omega_g (prose, no environment)

hypotheses.note: q != 0; the printed set is empty (achronalDomainPrinted_eq_empty)

finding: decided per class -- open for every elliptic and every parabolic g; for loxodromic g in normal form, open iff tau = 0 and L(g) has finite order on the orthogonal of the null frame (isOpen_achronalDomain_lox_iff)

findings: l.2024: the printed definition quantifies over all q in Z, including q = 0 where |g^0 x - x|^2 = 0, so Omega_g is empty as written; the intended reading is q != 0 (achronalDomainPrinted_eq_empty).

l.2026: 'It is the open set' is false in general; decided per class: open for every elliptic g (isOpen_achronalDomain_elliptic) and every parabolic g (isOpen_achronalDomain_parabolic); for loxodromic g in normal form (L(g) tau = tau), Omega_g is open iff tau = 0 and L(g) has finite order on the orthogonal of the null frame (isOpen_achronalDomain_lox_iff). Normal-form tau != 0 means g has no fixed point (lox_exists_fixed_iff); then Omega_g = {xy <= 0} is not open (witness boostShift_not_isOpen, d >= 2). For tau = 0 it fails exactly when some w orthogonal to the frame is not L(g)-periodic (e.g. an irrational rotation part, d >= 3; witness not formalized); the open case is inhabited by a pure boost (boostIsom_isOpen). Omega_g is an intersection of infinitely many open sets, which is why openness can fail.
questions: Omega_g is read with q != 0 (l.2024). Confirm.

labels.label: [7.E] elliptic case (prose)

hypotheses.paper: g x = R x + tau, R a rotation fixing tau (l.2031)
hypotheses.note: IsElliptic (L g) and L(g) tau = tau; the normal form is reachable by IsElliptic.exists_transConj_fixed

findings: l.2047-2049: confirmed; 'the R^n-fixed points' must read R^N for one N > 0 (not n the dimension): the periodic points are ker(L(g)^N - id), N = k! once ker(L(g)^{k!} - id) stabilises (exists_periodic_iff).

Survey caveat checked: it is the lightlike case of the paper's statement, not a defect: if L(g) has finite order every point is periodic and Omega_g is empty, tau != 0 null included (achronalDomain_elliptic_lightlike_of_pow_eq_one; witness achronalDomain_isomTrans_null).
l.2036: 'I which contains |(R^q - id)(x)|^2' should read '(R^q - id)(x)' (typo).

labels.label: [7.L] loxodromic case (prose)

hypotheses.paper: L(g)(x,y,v) = (lambda x, lambda^-1 y, R v), tau in R^{n-2} (l.2063-2070)
hypotheses.note: only null eigenvectors u, u' (eigenvalues lambda, lambda^-1, 0 < lambda != 1) of a minkQ-preserving L(g) with minkB u u' != 0, and L(g) tau = tau; tau in R^{n-2} follows, R is not assumed; achronalDomain_isLoxodromic supplies the frame from IsLoxodromic.frame
finding: true of interior(Omega_g); Omega_g itself equals {xy < 0} iff tau = 0 and L(g) has finite order on the frame's orthogonal

findings: l.2081 is inaccurate (DEC-27): the exact set is {xy < 0} union {xy = 0 and (tau != 0 or v not L(g)-periodic)} (mem_achronalDomain_lox_iff). For normal-form tau != 0 (equivalently: g has no fixed point, lox_exists_fixed_iff), Omega_g = {xy <= 0}, which is not open (achronalDomain_lox_of_ne_zero, not_isOpen_achronalDomain_lox); for tau = 0, Omega_g = {xy < 0} union {xy = 0, v not periodic} (achronalDomain_lox_of_eq_zero), and Omega_g = {xy < 0} (open) iff L(g) has finite order on the orthogonal of the frame (isOpen_achronalDomain_lox_iff). In every case interior(Omega_g) = {xy < 0} (interior_achronalDomain_lox), which is what the later use needs.

l.2068 and l.2075: the normalisations disagree: (lambda^q - 1)(lambda^-q - 1) = -4 sh^2(q log(lambda)/2), so lambda = e^{zeta/2} gives -4 sh^2(q zeta/4), and for the boost of rapidity zeta of l.1881-1887 lambda = e^zeta and the factor is -4 sh^2(q zeta/2), not -4 sh^2(q zeta). Harmless: only its sign and exponential growth are used (lox_factor_neg, exists_lox_dominates).

labels.label: [7.P] parabolic case (prose)

hypotheses.paper: tau fixed by R and in v1^perp (l.2092-2093)
hypotheses.note: R tau = tau only; tau orthogonal to v1 is never used

hypotheses.paper: parabolic: R a non-trivial elliptic element (l.1974)
hypotheses.note: reading inherited from Flat/Isometries (IsParabolic): R = id is admitted, as Sec. 9's purely unipotent case (l.2865) needs; plus U != id (strengthened reading, also inherited)
witnesses with R = id: linear nullRotIsom (Omega = complement of J^perp), tangent nullRotShift (Omega = M^n), transverse nullRotTime (tau = t, <t+e_i|t> = -1, Omega = empty)

findings: l.2109-2163 confirmed in all three cases, including the leading coefficient (q-1)(5-q)/12 |p tau|^2 of T(q) in the transverse case; the tangent conclusion (l.2138) needs only R tau = tau, not tau orthogonal to v1.

labels.label: blem:paranongh

hypotheses.note: false as printed: for d >= 3 (n >= 4) with R = id parabolic (IsParabolic admits it; Sec. 9's purely unipotent case l.2865 needs it), and for d >= 5 (n >= 6) with R != id required (l.1974, not_paranonghStrict); true for d <= 2 (paranongh_iff, paranonghPts_iff); tangent case: true for x0 off an affine hyperplane c + J^perp, false at c (paranongh_tangent)
R = id admitted (reading of Flat/Isometries); the strict reading IsParabolicNontrivR is also treated
reading: Paranongh counts exponents q, ParanonghPts counts distinct points g^q x; both are equivalent to d <= 2, and every positive result gives distinct points (IsAperiodic)

hypotheses.paper: 'in the future or in the past of x0'
hypotheses.note: CausallyRelated x0 (g^q x) = (minkowski d).le top in either direction, via le_top_iff_minkQ

findings: Lemma 7.1 (l.2173-2180) is FALSE as printed. (i) With 'parabolic' admitting R = id (Flat/Isometries' IsParabolic, as Sec. 9's purely unipotent case l.2865 requires), it fails for n >= 4 (d >= 3): g = (unit translation along x_k) o (null rotation in the (t, x_i, x_j) plane) has R = id, is parabolic, in Barbot's tangent case, Omega_g = M^n, and for x0 = 0 every x has only finitely many iterates causally related to x0, since |g^q x|^2 = |x|^2 + 2q<x|tau> + q^2|tau|^2 (nullRotShift_counterexample, not_paranongh). (ii) With 'parabolic' read as in Sec. 6.2 (l.1974, R non-trivial), it fails for n >= 6 (d >= 5): compose the same element with the half-turn in a plane orthogonal to t, x_i, x_j, x_k (halfTurnShift_counterexample, not_paranonghStrict); for n = 4, 5 a dimension count (R fixes the 4-dimensional I + <v_n> + <tau>, det R = 1) rules the tangent case out and the lemma would hold (not formalized). In reading (i) it holds exactly for n <= 3 (paranongh_iff, paranonghPts_iff), where the tangent case does not occur (Rem 6.1). Strongest true form, in every dimension: transverse, every x0 with x = x0 (paranongh_transverse); linear, every x0 (paranongh_linear); tangent, every x0 off an affine hyperplane c + J^perp, failing at x0 = c (paranongh_tangent), all with infinitely many distinct iterates.

Proof, l.2187-2188: |g^q x - x0|^2 = |x|^2 + |x0|^2 - 2<g^q x|x0> uses |g^q x|^2 = |x|^2, false unless g is linear (tau = 0); the dropped term grows like q^2|tau|^2 in the tangent case and is exactly what defeats the lemma. l.2191: <g^q x|x0> = <g^q x0|x> is false (for linear g it is <x|g^{-q} x0>). In the transverse case the true leading term of |g^q x - x0|^2 is quartic, -q^4|p tau|^2/12, not the cubic of l.2193; the conclusion survives.

Proof, l.2207-2209 (linear case): an x with <p^2(x)|x0> > 0 exists only if x0 is not in J^perp (p^2 x lies in J); that choice is paranongh_normal_of_not_mem. For x0 in J^perp the statement still holds but needs another choice: x = t u with u an R-fixed timelike vector, |t| large and sign(t) = sign<x0|p u>, since |g^q x - x0|^2 = |x - x0|^2 - 2q<x0|p x> (paranongh_linear_normal). Both choices give a point off J^perp, hence in Omega_g, hence with pairwise distinct iterates.

Use in Sec. 9 (l.2776-2783): 'select the base point x0 in S~' must avoid the exceptional affine hyperplane parallel to J^perp in the tangent case; a spacelike hypersurface is not contained in a null hyperplane, so the choice is possible, but the claim 'x can be selected up to Delta_0' is tied to the printed proof and is not checked here.
questions: Which corrected form of Lemma 7.1 should Sec. 9 rest on: (a) 'for every x0 off an affine hyperplane parallel to J^perp' (proved in all three cases, each transported to the whole class: paranongh_linear and paranongh_transverse for every x0, paranongh_tangent off c + J^perp), or (b) the printed statement restricted in dimension, which depends on the reading of 'parabolic': n <= 3 if R = id is admitted (as l.2865 needs), n <= 5 if R != id is required as at l.1974 (n >= 6 refuted and formalized; n = 4, 5 by a dimension count, not formalized)?

'Infinitely many g-iterates' (l.2177) is read in two ways: infinitely many exponents q (Paranongh) or infinitely many distinct points g^q x (ParanonghPts). They agree here (both iff d <= 2, and every positive construction has pairwise distinct iterates). Confirm that the points reading is the intended one.

'Causally related' is read as the ETT relation (minkowski d).le top in either direction (causal, not timelike). The printed proof aims at |g^q x - x0|^2 < 0; every positive result here gives a strict inequality for large q except the case x0 in J^perp of the linear case, where <= 0 is what is shown.

kb_proposals: For g : isom d, linOf g / trOf g are abbrevs for (g : AffineEquiv).linear and transPart; linOf g = linearPart g (linOf_eq_linearPart). g ^ n • x unfolds by pow_succ', mul_smul, smul_eq_lin_add, and LinearEquiv powers by pow_succ', LinearEquiv.mul_apply.

x ∈ minkOrth W is LinearMap.IsOrtho, which rw cannot see through: use Isometries' mem_minkOrth (Iff.rfl, ∀ w ∈ W, minkB w x = 0) or mem_minkOrth' — mem_minkOrth.1 hx _ hw : minkB w x = 0. No local helper needed.
An achronal domain is an intersection over q of open sets: check openness per class; for loxodromic g it holds iff tau = 0 and L(g) has finite order on the frame's orthogonal.

Polynomial-in-q asymptotics in this library: write minkQ of a combination with minkQ_smul_add3, substitute the vanishing pairings, finish with linear_combination using star_identity instances; exponential vs quadratic via tendsto_pow_const_div_const_pow_of_one_lt.

'Infinitely many iterates' has two readings (exponents vs points); prove the per-case results with IsAperiodic g x (from x ∈ Omega_g, or eventually g^n x ≠ x) and get the points reading by infinite_image_of_isAperiodic.
A rotation in SO0(1,d) without trigonometry: the half-turn x ↦ x − 2⟨x|e_a⟩e_a − 2⟨x|e_b⟩e_b is LinearEquiv.ofInvolutive, and det = 1 via det_eq_one_of_eq_sq with the quarter-turn (halfTurn_props).
